key_insight: Hardware benchmarks of one-dimensional Quantum Lattice Boltzmann show that collision and streaming dominate circuit cost, while sampler-based density reconstruction reduces measurement overhead.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies practical barriers to quantum fluid simulation without establishing a computational advantage over classical CFD.
method: Encode a one-dimensional advection–diffusion problem in quantum amplitudes.
Apply BGK-type collision and periodic-boundary streaming operators.
Reconstruct macroscopic density from computational-basis samples instead of full state tomography.
evidence_signal: Experiments on three IBM Quantum devices evaluate transpiled two-qubit gate counts, circuit depth, runtime, maximum absolute error, and RMSE, with sampler-based reconstruction preserving expected advection–diffusion dynamics.
watch_item: Results are limited to a one-dimensional benchmark, and collision and streaming costs remain scalability bottlenecks on current noisy hardware.
paper_title: Benchmarking One-Dimensional Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Methods on Quantum Hardware
